The hypothesis holds only narrowly: one estimator's new-quote hit rate stays well below their peers' after adjustment, while most of the other gaps come from customer mix, year or quote speed. I saved `prediction.json` before the first query, then `notes.md` and `finding.json`. Confidence is medium.

- **Estimator 115:** compared with other estimators quoting the same customer in the same year, 115 wins 7.1 points below expectation (389 comparable quotes, about 3.7 standard errors), while estimators 327 and 108 win 3.2 and 2.7 points above. The gap from 327 is 10.3 points (q238, q264).
- **It survives the obvious explanations:**
  - Still 6.4 points below with turnaround (RFQ received to quote sent) also held constant (q254).
  - Still 5.1 points below with part family held constant instead (q263).
  - Below expectation in all five customer segments and in most years from 2019 to 2024 (q241, q256).
- **Price and lead time aren't the cause.** Estimator 115's markup and lead weeks are close to their peers' (q245). Across all quotes in the same customer and year, neither markup nor lead weeks lines up with winning (q248).
- **Estimator 118's low rate is mix, not method.** Those quotes came in 2021–2022, when the whole shop was slow (46.4% of 2021 quotes took more than 8 days, hit rate 0.181). After adjustment, 118 is 2.3 points *above* expectation (q252, q254, q259).
- **Speed is the strongest pattern in the data.** Quotes sent within 0–2 days won 34.2%; those that took 8–30 days won 13.1% (q250). This is a correlation: slow quotes may just be the harder RFQs.
- **The two largest estimators are close.** Head to head with the same customers in the same years, 108 wins 3.0 points more than 109, under the 5-point threshold (q255).
- **Money:** at peer win rates, estimator 115's quotes would have won 27.7 more jobs. That is $257,449 of quoted value over 7.61 years, or $33,837 a year (q258). This is quoted value, not margin.

The records can't say why quotes were lost, how RFQs are assigned to estimators, or whether 115 follows up on open quotes. The standard errors are approximate: they ignore uncertainty in the peer rates and the clustering of quotes by customer. This is a pattern worth a conversation with estimator 115, not a judgement on them.

Next steps: review a sample of 115's lost and expired quotes against a peer's for the same customer and year. Start recording a loss reason when status is entered, and track quote turnaround as a shop measure.
